full_judgment: 3. Mr. Gour Gopal Saba with Mr. Md. Khurshid Alam Khan, the learned Advocates appeared for the appellants and Mr. J.K. Paul, the learned Advocate appeared for the State. At the out-set we have been taken through the F.I.R., the charge, the evidence, the 342 statements of the accused and other materials on record including the impugned judgment and order and then Mr. Saha the learned Advocate has seriously assailed the conviction and sentence of the accused-appellants on various grounds. It is firstly submitted by the learned Advocate for the appellants that the prosecution has totally failed to establish the charge under Sections 302/34 of the Penal Code as against each of the appellants by cogent, reliable and sufficient evidence beyond all reasonable doubt and as such the impugned judgment and order of conviction and sentence are liable to be set aside. In furtherance of the above submission, the learned Advocate contends that there has been major embellishment of the prosecution case as given in the F.I.R. and that the so called eye witnesses namely P.Ws. 1, 2 and 3 are highly interested and hence their evidences ought not to have been relied upon by the learned Additional Sessions Judge. Nextly it is contended that the F.I.R. did not disclose the name of any accused persons though it has been stated in the same that the informant Fazar Ali since dead lodged the F.I.R. after hearing about the occurrence from the alleged eye witnesses and further the said informant who of course could not be examined at the trial because of his death stated in his deposition before the committing court that he lodged the F.I.R. after hearing about the occurrence from the said witnesses, but the learned Additional Sessions Judge without considering this aspect of the matter and treating the deposition of the informant made before the enquiry Magistrate as a substantive evidence under Section 288 of the Code of Criminal Procedure wrongly relied upon the evidence of the so-called eye witnesses overlooking the major deviation and embellishment of the prosecution case and as a result there has been glaring miscarriage of justice. The next contention of Mr. Saha is that the recognition of the accused with the help of Kupi-bati and torch-light as claimed by the so-called eye-witnesses is highly improbable and doubtful in the facts and circumstances of the case and as such no conviction should have been based on such doubtful recognition of the accused. Further contention of the learned Advocate for the appellants is that there is substantial discrepancy between the post mortem report and the evidence on record with regard to the injuries alleged to have been caused by the accused persons on the victim and in such circumstances, the accused appellants ought to have been given benefit of doubt. It is further contended by the learned Advocate for the appellants that in a case like this where brutal murder of the victim has been alleged, the prosecution ought to have established the motive of the accused persons behind such murder and that having not been done by adducing reliable evidence by the prosecution the whole case against the accused appellants appears to have been shrouded with a mystery entitling them to get benefit of doubt. Lastly it is argued by the learned Advocate for the appellants that some material and charge sheeted witness's including one Makbul having not been examined in this case, the learned Additional Sessions Judge ought to have drawn an adverse presumption against the prosecution case.
